primary_source_applicability.source: Felsner, Lattice Structures from Planar Graphs (2004), Theorem 1
primary_source_applicability.supported: plane alpha-orientations with prescribed outdegrees form a distributive lattice under directed-cycle reversals
primary_source_applicability.missing_for_this_problem: the theorem uses the full alpha-orientation cycle-flip structure, not only root cycles whose pre-contraction endpoints lie on opposite rough arcs, and it does not assert normalized matching between this logical-parity split

primary_source_applicability.source: Propp, Lattice structure for orientations of graphs
primary_source_applicability.supported: orientations with fixed indegrees in a plane embedding admit a distributive-lattice structure under local moves
primary_source_applicability.missing_for_this_problem: internal local moves preserve the logical sector and are excluded from the public switching graph; distributivity alone does not supply the required restricted Hall inequalities

primary_source_applicability.source: Balachandran and Kush, The Normalized Matching Property in Random and Pseudorandom Bipartite Graphs
primary_source_applicability.supported: NMP is a scaled Hall condition, with results for independent random or Thomason-pseudorandom bipartite graphs
primary_source_applicability.missing_for_this_problem: the charge-conditioned switching graph is deterministic and highly dependent; no required pseudorandom edge-discrepancy hypothesis has been proved

primary_source_applicability.source: Khuller, Naor and Klein, The Lattice Structure of Flow in Planar Graphs
primary_source_applicability.supported: bounded integral planar circulations admit a distributive lattice via dual potentials and facial augmentation
primary_source_applicability.missing_for_this_problem: the result does not give normalized matching for a logical-parity subgraph restricted to opposite-rough-boundary path augmentations

precise_missing_lemma.structural: For every canonical square size and fixed interior charge, the bipartite graph of binary alpha-orientations joined only by directed root-cycle reversals connecting opposite rough arcs has the normalized matching property between logical sectors.
precise_missing_lemma.probabilistic: The normalized total minority mass 2^{-E} sum_Q min(N0(Q),N1(Q)) has a positive size-uniform lower bound (or positive liminf).
precise_missing_lemma.separation: the structural lemma identifies/saturates finite capacity; only the probabilistic lemma implies midpoint noncorrectability

decision.established: Fixed charge embeds exactly into planar alpha-orientations, and every L3/L4 charge-record switching graph satisfies normalized matching. All 18 single-edge and 153 double-edge deletions of canonical L4 with a crossing retain minority-sector matching saturation.
decision.theorem_mismatch: Published orientation/flow lattice theorems include internal cycle or face moves that our logical switching graph excludes; L4 has 578 ambiguous charge records split across multiple restricted components and 86528 states with an internal plaquette move.
decision.not_established: No reviewed theorem proves normalized matching for the restricted opposite-rough-arc root-cycle graph, and no canonical all-size proof or counterexample is obtained.
decision.threshold_claim: No square midpoint noncorrectability or decoding-threshold claim is promoted.
